target.title: fix(clawhub): decode promotions feed with fatal UTF-8 validation
target.body:
## Summary

Decode the ClawHub promotions feed with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw immediately, instead of silently becoming U+FFFD in a payload that is then written to the local cache and reused via etag revalidation.

## What Problem This Solves

`fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed` downloads the promotions feed (`/api/v1/feeds/promotions`) and returns both the parsed feed and the raw `payload` string. The caller (`maybeRefreshPromotionsFeed` in `src/infra/promotions-feed.ts`) persists that payload together with the response etag into the local state store, and later revalidates with `If-None-Match`.

- The body is decoded with a forgiving `TextDecoder` (default `fatal: false`), so invalid bytes are silently replaced with U+FFFD.
- When the corruption lands inside a JSON string value, `JSON.parse` still succeeds and the feed passes schema validation.
- The corrupted payload is written to the cache with the etag; subsequent `304 Not-Modified` revalidations keep reusing the corrupted snapshot — one transient corruption becomes permanently cached, and corrupted promotion text can surface to users.

**Code evidence**: at [clawhub.ts:1950](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L1950), `new TextDecoder().decode(buffer)` decodes the feed response without UTF-8 validation.

## Root Cause

- Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing.
- Feed schema validation (`parseClawHubPromotionsFeed`) checks structure and field types, but operates on the already-decoded string, so it cannot detect byte-level corruption after U+FFFD substitution.
- Invariant violated: "feed response bytes are always valid UTF-8" — not guaranteed for bytes served through a CDN edge or proxy.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to the decoder:

- Invalid bytes now throw a `TypeError` before parsing and before the payload can be cached. The caller's established fail-silent catch treats it exactly like an offline or malformed response: cached state stays untouched (only the attempt timestamp advances), so a corrupted snapshot is never persisted and the next cadence retries cleanly.
- This is the same pattern already used for provider JSON bodies in `readProviderJsonResponse` ([provider-http-errors.ts:344](src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts#L344)).
- Alternative considered: validating the decoded payload for U+FFFD before caching — rejected, because U+FFFD can be legitimate content and post-hoc scanning cannot distinguish corruption from real data.

## User Impact

- **Before**: a corrupted feed response is cached with its etag and reused indefinitely; promotion text containing `�` can be shown to users until the etag changes upstream.
- **After**: the corrupted response is rejected before caching; the previous cached snapshot (if any) stays in effect and the next check retries the download.

## Evidence

- **Before** (upstream/main): `feed accepted, first entry title: "�Free Example models"` — **FAIL**: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD in the cached feed payload
- **After** (with fix): `feed rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8` — **PASS**: corrupted feed response rejected before caching

## Real Behavior Proof

Proof serves a promotions feed body containing a raw `0xFF` byte inside a promotion title from a real local HTTP server, then calls the real `fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed` against it via its `baseUrl` override.

### Before (on main)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
feed accepted, first entry title: "�Free Example models"
FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD in the cached feed payload
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
feed rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
PASS: corrupted feed response rejected before caching
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` — 21 passed (20 existing + 1 new)
- New regression test: `rejects a promotions feed response with invalid UTF-8 bytes`
- `tsgo:core` typecheck passed; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback
- existing direct Proposal-ID lifecycle calls remain compatible

## Evidence

- Before the history squash, the focused service, policy, agent-tool, and CLI suites passed on `2809501786e2a62422e4abff405ef453d8c6f4eb` (47 + 9 + 26 + 3 tests), along with build, type, lint, formatting, docs, and `git diff --check` validation.
- The squashed head `9da2cb160445685277384676935215111cfbdba8` has the exact same tree (`d16313599b68c80b383d1a9b58fc1682a3f01ab8`) as `2809501786e2a62422e4abff405ef453d8c6f4eb`. The binary diff against the pre-squash base is unchanged, `git diff --check` passes, and the PR range contains one commit.
- Fresh [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29669306891) passed for the squashed head. In the initial fresh [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29669306898) attempt, 55 jobs succeeded and 11 were skipped; one unrelated ACP CLI process-test shard hit its two 5-second help-command timeouts, and the CI gate propagated that result. A failed-job rerun requires upstream repository admin rights.
- Repeated structured autoreview found and fixed approval-parameter preservation, caught the TOCTOU risk in an attempted alternative, and reported the final pre-squash branch and formatting fix clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Permanent [Mantis Telegram Desktop proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29156925613) covers create/update review, pagination, first-page lifecycle controls, approval/rejection, and stale-version rejection. The [artifact index](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-103872/run-29156925613-1/index.json) retains the native screenshots and motion proof.
- The broad remote `pnpm check:changed` lane could not start from the original validation host because the configured Blacksmith client was absent. GitHub CI remains the broad remote gate.

## Verification

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
  src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts \
  src/cli/skills-cli.workshop.test.ts

pnpm build
pnpm tsgo
pnpm check
pnpm docs:lint

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

Squash integrity checks:

```bash
git rev-parse 2809501786e2a62422e4abff405ef453d8c6f4eb^{tree}
git rev-parse 9da2cb160445685277384676935215111cfbdba8^{tree}
git diff --exit-code 2809501786e2a62422e4abff405ef453d8c6f4eb 9da2cb160445685277384676935215111cfbdba8
git rev-list --count 00eb33fe8e6ebf278ad052f0cbbb257318d78323..9da2cb160445685277384676935215111cfbdba8
git diff --check 00eb33fe8e6ebf278ad052f0cbbb257318d78323...9da2cb160445685277384676935215111cfbdba8
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: preview the exact canonical result of a Skill Workshop proposal before approval and bind the later lifecycle decision to that reviewed version.

Real environment tested: live Telegram DM on deployed production integration `ef2acbbe69b52f92c788188de3b159de92ad24ef`. The final pre-squash changes after the recorded behavior proof documented the existing version-binding invariant, aligned formatting/tests after rebases, and did not change the demonstrated runtime flow.

Exact steps exercised: review a paginated create proposal and its first-page Approve/Reject/Next controls; revise v1 to v2 and attempt approval from the stale v1 prompt; review and approve the fresh v2 prompt; review an update proposal's unified diff and reject it.

Permanent evidence:

- [Mantis run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29156925613)
- [candidate screenshot](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-103872/run-29156925613-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.png)
- [candidate GIF](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-103872/run-29156925613-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.gif)
- [candidate MP4](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-103872/run-29156925613-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.mp4)
- [raw artifact index](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-103872/run-29156925613-1/index.json)

The Mantis candidate was captured at `d5c1be51d406858d447fa97658ca72bdb1ad8872`; it is retained as permanent behavior proof, while the fresh GitHub runs above validate the current squashed head.

Observed result: create approval succeeds only for the reviewed current version; stale approval fails closed with expected-v1/current-v2 feedback; update review shows the unified diff; Approve and Reject remain available from page 1.

What was not tested: a separate burner-account Crabbox run. The behavior was instead exercised end-to-end in the deployed production integration used by the operator.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the change, ran focused validation, completed repeated code-review passes, and performed the history-only squash. No agent transcript is attached.
